_comment: What the plugin's bootstrap is allowed to fetch, and nothing else.
`owner` and `repo` are the one repository this product is published from. They are
not decoration: the update check reads them back out of the URL GitHub redirects to
and refuses anything under a different owner or a different repository, so a
redirect that leaves this project cannot answer the question.
`download` and `archive` build the one URL shape an install may fetch. An ordinary
install fetches the version in .codex-plugin/plugin.json and nothing else, so a
plugin at a given version can fetch that version's archive alone. There are two
exceptions, and both are narrow. The version `-Update` fetches is not an input: it is
three integers read from the redirect above. `-Version` fetches the pre-release a
person said yes to when the check offered it, accepted only in this product's own
grammar and rebuilt from its integers and one of two words, and only when it is newer
than what is installed. Every check below still applies to what comes back.
`latest` is asked only when a person asks for it - `-CheckOnly` or `-Update`. It is
requested with HEAD, so no body is transferred, and no body is parsed either: the
answer is the path of the URL the request ends at.
`sha256` maps a version to the digest of its published archive. A version listed here
is verified against that digest and the published .sha256 sidecar is not consulted at
all. A version that is absent, or null, falls back to the sidecar - which is weaker,
and the bootstrap says so out loud rather than implying a guarantee it does not have.
An update is normally the weaker case: a release published after this plugin was
written cannot have been pinned before it existed.
A version has no entry here until its archive exists, and the key is added afterwards:
the digest cannot be known before the archive exists. The executables inside are
reproducible from v0.6.0 - build/normalize_pe.py replaces the two fields the in-box
compiler varies. The measured compiler and machine scope is recorded in VERIFY.md;
so the digest is still taken from the published file rather than from a local
rebuild. CONTRIBUTING.md carries that as a release step.
`releases` is the one list `-CheckOnly` reads besides: GitHub's list of this
repository's ten newest releases, asked once github.com has answered `latest`, with
GET, unauthenticated, and no redirect followed. It is the one body the bootstrap parses,
and all it takes from it is the newest published pre-release newer than both the
installed version and `latest`, which the check offers and never installs on its own.
`release_pages` is the same list on the same host and path, a page of thirty at a time,
and `{page}` is the one thing put into it. Only the Dashboard's Install another version...
reads it (`-Versions`, and `-Pick` again before it installs), at most five pages, when a
person presses that button and when they confirm a version. It takes from each release
its tag, whether it is a draft or a pre-release, and the names of its files - nothing
else - and the version picked is still fetched by `download` and `archive` and checked
as an install is.
`prerelease` names the version under development once it is tagged and published as a
GitHub pre-release. `latest` never answers with one and it carries no digest, so the
pin test excuses it; it may name that version alone, which empties it at the next bump.
A pre-release is installed only when a person says yes to the check's offer (`-Version`,
which asks `latest` and `releases` again first and installs only what they would still
offer), and then against the .sha256 published beside it, since none is ever pinned here.
`advanced` is the advanced edition's archive and its digests, from the version in
`since` on. The keys above stay the standard edition's, because every published
bootstrap reads `archive` and `sha256` from its own copy of this file and has to go on
finding the standard archive under the name it has always built. The advanced name is
a second constant rather than a variation of the first, so which edition is fetched
only ever chooses between two fixed templates; its `sha256` is kept exactly as the one
above is, and a version is pinned in both in the same commit.
